# Information Transformation Control Tower - Workshop Playbook
> Generic information-architecture / DMS template informed by a supplied workbench prototype. Fictional cases only.

## Objective
Turn observed files and repositories into governed information with clear business meaning, process ownership, lifecycle, classification, confidentiality and retention. Do not assume the target must replicate existing folders.

## Ten workshops
| ID | Topic | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WS-01 | Mission & Governance Alignment | Scope charter, RACI, decision log |
| WS-02 | Repository Discovery | AS-IS inventory and anomalies |
| WS-03 | Documentary Process & Lifecycle | Process/document lifecycle map |
| WS-04 | Taxonomy & Classification | Canonical term and document-class catalog |
| WS-05 | Access Intent & Security | Role/access matrix and exceptions |
| WS-06 | Records & Retention | Records-class decisions and legal review |
| WS-07 | TO-BE Information Model | Target IA, libraries and metadata |
| WS-08 | Migration Mapping & Disposition | Map, archive, exclude and HOLD decisions |
| WS-09 | Pilot Readiness & UAT | Sample, test cases, readiness gate |
| WS-10 | Closure & Benefits | Acceptance and measured outcomes |

## Workshop conduct
Frame purpose and exclusions. Bring only approved representative examples. Ask what a document proves, who owns it, who consumes it, its trigger and lifecycle. Challenge the proposed mapping and capture counterexamples. Finish with a signed list of decisions and open items.

## Evidence discipline
Record source vocabulary separately from a canonical taxonomy. Statuses: CONFIRMED, RECOMMENDED or TO VALIDATE. Keep HOLD and records-management decisions separate from technical archiving proposals.

## AS-IS baseline
Location, document class, process, owner, volume when known, active or historical status, technical/ROT candidate, confidentiality, observed access and retention clues.

## TO-BE design
For each class decide primary process, target repository, site/library, metadata, views, owner, access, disposition, workflow and source-of-truth relationship. Do not duplicate operational master systems inside a document library.

## Pilot readiness
Confirm scope, representative sample, mapping exceptions, permissions, security reviews, backup, rollback and measurable acceptance criteria. An unknown critical permission or unresolved retention decision blocks sign-off.

## Chain of traceability
Source -> observation -> decision -> business requirement -> target decision -> UAT case -> evidence -> approval. Record who validated each link.

## Limitations
Workshop titles reflect the structure observed in the supplied v1.7 prototype. This guide does not assert any real client retention schedules, group processes or folder mapping.
